November 25, 1936.    Morning Translation.

"At about 10 a.m. yesterday (November 19)
a pedestrian, an old man of more than 70 years of age,
was knocked down at the corner of Pingliang and Glen
Roads by a motor car (licence number unknown) which
was moving at a high speed. Upon finding that he had
caused an accident, the driver drove off at a high
speed. Later, a post duty policeman conveyed the
injured man to the Sacred Heart Hospital where the man
succumbed to his injuries soon after arrival."
It is known to everybody that there is a Police
Station at the corner of Pingliang and Glen Roads. Moreover,
the accident occurred opposite the Station. The place is
not an isolated locality. It is customary to have a
policeman on duty at the front gate of Police Station; the
accident happened at about 10 O'clock in the morning; yet
the motor car was driven off unnoticed after the accident.
I am of the opinion that an explanation should
be demanded from the Police authorities. We should not
overlook the matter just because the deceased was a poor
old man, for it is a case that concerns not only the
deceased but the general public as well.

Morning Translation.

Hwa Mei an Pao dated Nov.23:

SEVEN PROMINENT RESIDENTS ARRESTED ON GRAVE CHARGES

Mr. Sung Chun Shih (沈儒), native of
Kashing, age 63, residing at House No.51, Lane No.1292 Yu
Yuen Road, member of the Standing Committee of the Shanghai
Bar Association, Mr. Wang Chao Shih (王造時), native of
Kiangsi Province, age 34, residing at House No.7 Tifeng
Road, and Mr. Soo Chi Lien (沙千里), native of Huchow, age
33, both lawyers and members of the Bar Association,
and Mr. Li Kung Pu (李公樸), native of Zangchow, age 35,
residing at House No.24, Lane No.1736, Yu Yuen Road, President
of the Liang Tsai School (量才學校), are all prominent
members of the Federation of National Salvation Associations.
On November 22, members of the Bureau of Public
Safety called at the Bubbling Well Police Station of the
International Settlement, produced an official dispatch and
requested assistance to effect the arrest of these four
persons for some political offence. Warrants of arrest
were obtained from the Shanghai First Special District Court
by the Bubbling Well Police Station. Messrs. Sung Chun
Shih, Wang Chao Shih and Li Kung Pu were arrested in Bubbling
Well district late at night by a party of detectives and
uniformed policemen under Foreign Detective Sub-Inspector
"Caley". Lawyer Soo Chi Lien who lives in Sinza District
was arrested with the assistance of Sinza Police Station.
The four arrested persons were arraigned before
Judge Nyi Chung Nee (聶重義) of the Second Branch of the
Kiangsu High Court at 9 a.m. November 23. The proceedings
were held in camera. Only Mr. King S. Kum, the Municipal
Advocate, the lawyers for the defence and the police officers
in charge of the case were present.
After a lengthy interrogation, Judge Nyi allowed
the accused to be released on bail furnished by their
respective lawyers. Messrs. Chang Yi Fan (張以藩),
Ngoh Goong (吳森) and Chen Tse Kao (陳志皋) are
appearing for Mr. Li Kung Pu; Messrs. Yu Chung Loh (俞鍾輅)
and Li Yung Chi (李文池) for Mr. Wang Chao Shih; Messrs.
Chang Yao Tseng (張耀曾) and Chen Tse Kao for Mr. Sung
Chun Shih; Messrs. Tsai Loh Zung (蔡天東), Yang Tien Sung
(楊天遜) and Aung Pao Chi (汪葆楫) for Mr. Soo Chi Lien.
All the guarantors were instructed to produce the accused
at the next hearing which will take place at 2 p.m.
November 25. The representatives of the Bureau of Public
Safety requested the extradition of the accused.
At the request of the Bureau of Public Safety,
the French Municipal Police have arrested Miss Sze Liang
(史良), a lawyer, Mr. Chow Tao Feng (鄒奮), Editor-
in-Chief of the "Livelihood Sunday Weekly", and Mr. Chang
Nan Chi (章乃器), an economist, on a similar charge.
The arrested persons were arraigned before
the Third Branch of the Kiangsu High Court at 3 p.m.
November 23. Messrs. Chang Tse Niang (張志讓) and Tong Hwa
(唐豪) are appearing for Mr. Chang Nan Chi and Miss Sze
Liang; Mr. Sung Tso Chi (孫祖基) for Mr. Chow Tao Feng.
It is learned that they will likewise be released on bail.

families of the various accused by a reporter of this paper:-

November 13, 1936.

Shanghai Various Circles National Salvation Federation
- convenes meetings in celebration of the birthday of
the late Kuomintang Leader.

The Shanghai Various Circles National Salvation
Federation convened a meeting of members of local national
salvation associations in the Chinese Y.W.C.A., 999 Bubbling
Well Road, at 1 p.m. November 12, ostensibly to celebrate the
birthday of the late Kuomintang leader Dr. Sun Yat-sen.

A large number of Chinese consisting of students,
labourers and shop assistants proceeded to the Ningpo Fellow
Countrymen's Association, 480 Yu Ya Ching Road, between 12
noon and 1 p.m. November 12, but upon arrival there were
informed by pickets that the Police and officials of the
Association had forbidden the meeting there, and were instructed
to proceed to the Chinese Y.W.C.A., the second meeting place.
By 2 p.m. about 800 persons had entered the compound of the
Y.W.C.A. and at that time the meeting was formally opened.
A presidium consisting of the following persons was formed :-

Li Kung-poh (李公樸), Principal of the Liang Zai
Supplementary School, Continental Emporium
Building, Nanking Road, and one of the leading
members of the Vocational Circles National
Salvation Association.

Tsang Mai-chi (章乃器), ex-Sub-Manager of the Chekiang
Industrial Bank, and a leading member of the
Cultural Circles National Salvation Association.

Wong Chao-dzu (王造時), a lawyer by profession,
living at 7B Tifeng Road, a leading member of the
Cultural Circles National Salvation Association.

Sung Chun-dzu (沈鈞儒), a lawyer by profession, living
at 5 Tao Yuan Fang, Yu Yuen Road, and concurrently
Dean of the Shanghai Law College, Kiangwan Road. He
is a leading member of the Cultural Circles National
Salvation Association.

Sz Liang (史良), a female lawyer, living at 1
Lafayette Terrace, Rue Lafayette. A leading member
of the Women's Circles National Salvation Association.

Soo Chien-li (沙千里), a lawyer by profession with
an office at the Tsung Chen (宗誠) Building,
Kiukiang Road. A committee member of the Ants' Club
(Ants' Club), Room 420 Continental Emporium Building,
Nanking Road, and concurrently a leading member of
the Vocational Circles National Salvation Association.

- 2 -

Yang Ching-sai (楊經才), a supervisor in the Tien Yih
(天一) Insurance Company, 255 Peking Road. A
leading member of the Vocational Circles National
Salvation Association.

After the formal opening of the meeting, those
present sang two songs entitled "March of Volunteer Armies
(義勇軍進行曲) and "Beat them back home" (打回老家去)
(the latter song is anti-Japanese in nature). Li Kung-poh
then made a speech eulogizing the deeds and spirit of the late
Dr. Sun Yat-sen. He stated that the object of the meeting
apart from celebrating the anniversary was to induce the
authorities to cease concluding secret agreements with Japan
and advocated that the nation should be saved in accordance
with the instructions of the late leader.

The second speaker was Tsang Hai-chi, who stated
that China should unite with Great Britain, the United States,
France and Soviet Russia and form a group to ensure the safety
of China against Japan.

Wong Chao-dzu followed, and made a speech stating
that the late Kuomintang leader advocated that a treaty should
be concluded with Soviet Russia, that the Communist Party
should be allowed in China, and agriculture and industry should
be developed. He continued to say that the present Chinese
Government had ignored these instructions and therefore China
suffered from foreign aggression.

Sung Chun-dzu (沈鈞儒) was the next speaker. He
also advocated the policies mentioned above as the means to
save China from ruin. He also remarked that Dr. Sun Yat-sen
had praised Lenin and as conditions in Soviet Russia were
had
excellent, Dr. Sun Yat-sen/been right. He said that no power
in the world could break Soviet Russia. He concluded that
China should unite with the Communist Party in compliance
with the instructions of Dr. Sun. He was of the opinion that
the Government should forthwith suspend the anti-Communist
campaign.

- 3 -

Sz Liang was the fifth speaker. She stated that the
Chinese Government should not prohibit the people from taking
part in the national salvation movement at the present
critical time and that all the Chinese irrespective of parties
should unanimously resist Japan. She remarked that according
to the instructions of Dr. Sun, the Government should protect
the people in the national salvation movement but the present
government, she continued, not only refrained from protecting
the people, but oppressed them.

At this point, an invitation was issued to those
present to deliver speeches. Two female workers named Fang
Dzu (方 氏) and Liu Tsao-dee (劉招弟), claiming to be in the
employ of the Dah Kong Cotton Mill, accepted the invitation.
Fang Dzu reported that the workers of Japanese cotton mills
had gone on strike to demand an increase in wages and that some
workers had been taken to a small room by the Japanese
management. She described that one of these workers had been
killed by the Japanese and her body put in a sack and thrown
into the Wangpoo. At this juncture, the audience commenced
to shout slogans including "Overthrow the Japanese Imperialists"
and "Assist the Strikers." Liu Tsao-dee, the next speaker,
made another speech depicting how the workers were cruelly
exploited by the capitalists and requested the attendance to
render assistance to the workers.

Tsang Kai-chi again took the platform and informed
the crowd that Madame Sun Yat-sen had intended to be present
to deliver a speech, but was prevented by illness. He read
the following speech written by her.

"In commemoration of the late Dr. Sun Yat-sen, brethren
throughout the nation should continue to struggle for the
emancipation of the Chinese race. At present, we should
realize that our greatest enemies are the Japanese
Imperialists and Chinese traitors."

- 4 -

"We should unite with all nations who are lovers of
peace and form an international league against invasion,
especially by allying with Great Britain, U.S.A., France,
and Soviet Russia to ensure collective safety on the Pacific
and to oppose the Japanese imperialists. We should ally
with the peace-loving masses of Japan, Korea and Formosa
and form a united international battle line to overthrow the
Fascist militarists of Japan. We should unite all parties
and classes to form a united battle line for the purpose of
overthrowing the Japanese imperialists.

"The three policies of Dr. Sun indicate the above
plans. We should go forward bravely. Steel and blood
will certainly accomplish the glorious enterprise for the
emancipation of the race."

Tsang Nai-chi concluded by saying that the people
should of their own accord rise and save their nation despite
obstruction from the Government.

Wong Chao-dz then took the platform and read the
following proposals to the crowd, which were duly passed :
1) That the attendance should contribute money to support
the strikers of Japanese cotton mills.
2) That the Government be requested to cease concluding secret
agreements with Japan, but to send troops to the North
to assist the anti-Japanese troops at Suiyuan.
3) That a delegation be appointed to proceed to the North
and to convey good wishes to the anti-Japanese armies at
Suiyuan.
4) That the Government be requested to unite with Great
Britain, United States of America, France and Soviet Russia
and form an international league against Japan.

- 5 -

5) That a circular telegram be despatched informing
the people throughout China of the minutes of this
meeting.
Wong Chao-dzu then submitted to the meeting the
following proposals made by the Shanghai Municipality
Students Circles National Salvation Association :-
1) That the Government release all students arrested
in connection with the national salvation Movement.
2) That the authorities of various universities be
induced to take back those students dismissed in
connection with the national salvation movement.
3) That the Government be urged to enforce special
education during times of national crisis.
The following resolutions proposed by members
of the audience were then discussed and passed :-
1) That funds be raised by public subscription on behalf
of the strikers in a three days' campaign commencing
on November 13.
2) That Groups be formed to sympathize with the strikers
in Japanese cotton mills.
3) That a demand be submitted for the release of workers
arrested in connection with the strike in Japanese
cotton mills, failing which a general strike be
declared.
4) That the General Labour Union be requested to call
for a strike of all labourers in Shanghai, in sympathy
with the Japanese cotton mill strikers.
5) That a "Japanese Mill Strikers' Support Committee" be
formed consisting of two representatives from each local
public body.

- 6 -
6. That a circular telegram be despatched asking Chinese
at home and abroad to render assistance to the strikers
in Japanese cotton mills.
7. That anti-Japanese propaganda groups be formed in
connection with the strike of the Japanese cotton mills.
8. That the anti-Communist campaign undertaken by the
National Government be opposed.
Finally it was decided to refer all these regulations
to the members of the presidium for execution. The meeting
was concluded at 4 p.m. when the following slogans were shouted:-
1. Support the anti-Japanese troops in Suiyuan.
2. Urge the government to issue a general mobilization
order at once in order to resist Japan.
3. Oppose the co-operation of China and Japan in the anti-
communist campaign, and demand the immediate suspension
of the communist suppression campaign.
4. Ally with Great Britain, U.S.A., France and Soviet Russia
to ensure collective safety on the Pacific.
5. Unite various parties in the country to resist foreign
aggression.
6. Let Chinese and Japanese masses unite and overthrow the
Japanese Imperialists.
7. Urge the Kuomintang to restore the National revolutionary
spirit of the late Dr. Sun Yat-sen.
8. Oppose the Government's connivance at the Japanese
invasion into North China.
9. The revolutionary spirit of the late Dr. Sun Yat-sen
is immortal !
10. Long live the emancipation of the Republic of China.

- 7 -

While the crowd which towards the close of the
meeting numbered approximately 1,000 persons was dispersing,
persons were posted at an inner gate of the Y.M.C.A. premises
and collected subscriptions in support of the strikers of
Japanese cotton mills. A total sum of $200 was raised.

During the proceedings, copies of two kinds of
literature were distributed among the attendance. One is
entitled "Special Issue of the National Salvation Intelligence
in commemoration of the birthday of the late Dr. Sun Yat-sen."
It contains the speech of Madame Sun Yat-sen and the ten slogans
referred to above. The other, a handbill, contains a
manifesto purporting to emanate from the Shanghai Municipality
Students Circles National Salvation Association bearing on the
commemoration of the birthday of the late Kuomintang leader.
This handbill advocates that the Government should

1. Carry out Dr. Sun's revolutionary policies.
2. Assist the anti-Japanese troops at Suiyuan.
3. Enforce "Too Yuan" (?) diplomacy.
4. Protect the freedom of patriotic movements.

Also present at the meeting were ten plain-clothes
members of the Bureau of Public Safety and Mr. and Mrs. Max
Granich. Max Granich is the editor of the reactionary
publication entitled "Voice of China."

Afternoon Translation.

China Times and other local newspapers:

THE CASE AGAINST THE NATIONAL SALVATION LEADERS

No news has yet been received as to the date for the next hearing of the case against Sung Chun-dz (沈鈞儒), Tsang Nai-chi (章乃器), Li Kung-poh (李公樸), Wong Zao-dz (王造時), Tseu Tao-fun (鄒韜奮), Soo Chi-li (沙千里) and Sz Liang (史良), the seven leaders of the National Salvation Association. The case was last heard on June 25 and was remanded for the purpose of obtaining a file from the Military Affairs Commission.

During the period of remand, numerous friends of Sung Chun-dz and the others, as well as many bona fide persons working for national salvation, requested the authorities to withdraw the charges or quickly to pronounce Sung and the others not guilty on the ground that the advocacy of the prisoners for unification and resistance against aggression did not in any way contradict the policy of the National Government. It is said that the Presiding Judge in this case is making a thorough examination of the evidence produced by the procurator, such as the Manifesto of the Inaugural Meeting of the All-China National Salvation Federation, a publication entitled "Some Fundamental Conditions and Minimum Demands Regarding Unification and Resistance against Aggression" etc., in order to eliminate misinterpretation of the texts.

Although it was alleged by the procurator that Sung Chun-dz and the others had instigated the Sian Incident, it is learned that the file kept by the Military Affairs Commission in connection with the case of Chang Hsueh-liang does not contain anything which may prove any conspiracy between the arrested persons and military officers. After the Lukouchiao Incident occurred, the seven arrested persons sent a joint telegram to General Chiang Kai-shek supporting the latter's views regarding the incident. This shows that their patriotic sentiments are unchanged. It is thought that the authorities will not incarcerate the national salvation leaders in prison much longer.

Chuin Chung Sin Wan (群衆新聞):

PEOPLE'S LECTURE GROUP FORMED TO EDUCATE PEASANTS

In view of the fact that 90% of the Chinese, especially the peasants and villagers, are uneducated and have no national understanding, Niao Chung-ying (倪仲英), Zang Tso-ming (常竹銘), Hung Kuo-hwei (洪國煒) and other Chinese youths in this locality have formed a body known as the "People's Group to Lecture on Aversion of the Nation from Extinction". The group in question has some 30 members, both male and female, who undergo training between 3 and 10 p.m. daily. Many people from various local circles have joined the organization.

Chun Chung Sin Wan (群衆週刊) :-
MADAME SUN YAT-SEN AND MANY OTHERS SUPPORT NATIONAL SALVATION
With a view to backing their opinion that
it is not a crime to work for national salvation, Madame
Sun Yat-sen and 15 others have promoted a movement to
surrender themselves to prison for national salvation.
It is learned that up till now, more than
2,000 persons, including members of every walk of life,
have joined into this movement. It is to be noted that
this movement was promoted for the purpose of bringing about
the release of the seven arrested leaders of the National
Salvation Association as well as for struggling for the
decision that it is not a crime to work for the salvation
of the nation.

July 8, 1937.

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers (Soochow Telegram) :-
THE CASE AGAINST THE NATIONAL SALVATION LEADERS : PERIOD
FOR THEIR DETENTION EXTENDED

Sung Chun-dz (沈儒) and the six
others, who are charged with offences against internal
security of the State, received on July 6 the following
judgment from the Kiangsu High Court as regards the
extension of their detention period:-
"The accused in this case, who are
charged with offences against the internal security of
the Republic, have been under detention in this Court
since April 5 last. However, despite the fact that the
three months' detention period has expired, the
investigation into the evidence of this case is still
incomplete and it is, therefore, necessary to prolong
the period of the detention of the accused. Consequently,
the period of their detention is extended for a further
period of two months as from July 5 in accordance with
the provisions of Article 108, Sections 1 and 2, of the
Code of Criminal Procedure."
Upon receipt of this judgment, the
accused requested the Kiangsu High Court to resume the
hearing of the case as soon as possible on the ground
that they had already been under detention for a
considerable length of time.

Eastern Daily News (東方日報) of July 6 :-

Settlement Film Censorship Abolition Movement

The other day about 10 cultural bodies in
Shanghai held a meeting at which it was decided to form
a committee to undertake the work of abolishing the film
and drama censorship in the Settlement.
We cannot achieve our end merely by holding
meetings and issuing manifestoes and circular telegrams.
We have already said that it is not a difficult task to
abolish the censorship; the exhibition of the film "The
New Earth" in defiance of the censorship supports our
contention. The first thing to do is to ask ourselves

Abolition Movement Committee in stock besides holding

July 7, 1937.
Afternoon Translation.

Tien Hsia Daily News (天下日報) (Soochow correspondence) :-

MADAME SUN YAT-SEN AND NATIONAL SALVATION LEADERS

On the morning of July 5, Madame Sun Yat-sen and ten others left Shanghai by train for Soochow and arrived there at 9.14 a.m. They proceeded to the High Court and called on Mr. Chu Shih-sung (朱树声), the President, and Mr. Sung Hung-ling (孙鸿霖), the Chief Procurator of the Court.

In view of the fact that they had been engaged in the work for national salvation together with Sun Chun-dz and the six other national salvation leaders, Madame Sun and the others requested that they themselves be detained and tried with Sung and the others.

President Chu replied that he was in sympathy with the patriotism of the callers, but that in the capacity of President, he could not interfere in the trial of the case. He added that the demand submitted by the callers for their detention should be made to the Chief Procurator.

Madame Sun and the others repeated the request for their detention before the Chief Procurator. The Chief Procurator replied that the case against Sung Chun-dz and the others had not yet been concluded and that it was hard to surmise the judgment of the case. So it was not necessary, the Chief Procurator added, to answer their request. He advised the callers to return to Shanghai and then left owing to pressure of work.

As no result had been obtained, Madame Sun and the other callers remained at the Court. The Court does not open in the afternoon at present and no one appeared to see the callers until nightfall. The callers therefore prepared bedding, food and mosquito extermination incense for the purpose of remaining at the Court for the night, until a definite reply had been given by the Court.

At 6.30 p.m. the President of the Court sent Procurator Hsia to open negotiations with the callers and explained the difficulties of the Court. Finally, the following four points were discussed and made definite :-
1) That the National Salvation Association be recognized as having not committed a crime.
2) That the request submitted by the callers be investigated.
3) That the Court accept and deal with any evidence submitted by Madame Sun and others.
4) That similar action be taken if any other members of the National Salvation Association submit a request for investigation.

The abovementioned four points were written on paper and President Chu and Procurator indicated their agreement with them. Madame Sun and the others then left the Court for Shanghai at 8 p.m. the same day.

Madame Sun intends to submit evidence for investigation by the Court.

July 6, 1937.

Morning Translation.

China Times and other local newspapers:

EXCHANGE SHOP OWNERS' ASSOCIATION TO DEAL WITH TRAITOROUS MEMBERS

The other day, the Money Exchange Shop Owners' Association received a letter from the Chinese Chamber of Commerce to the effect that recently the Yokohama Specie Bank, the Bank of Taiwan, and other Japanese banks received large quantities of banknotes of the "Central Bank of Manchukuo" and entrusted the Hung Kong (鴻康) and five other exchange shops to act as agents for the exchange of these banknotes.

Yesterday, the Executive Committee of the Money Exchange Shop Owners' Association held an urgent meeting owing to the fact that the Hung Kong and two others of the six exchange shops are members of the Association, and it was considered that measures to stop such action on the part of their members should be devised.

Upon reading a report from the "Lih Pao" to the effect that they were acting as agents for the Japanese banks to undertake the exchange of "Manchukuo" banknotes, the Hung Kong and two other exchange shops, who are members of the Association, were greatly surprised and immediately sent a joint letter to the Association stating that they had nothing to do with the matter and requesting that an investigation be carried out.

An investigation conducted by the Association reveals that the report is absolutely untrue.

Fearing that traitorous merchants may privately undertake the exchange of "Manchukuo" banknotes, the Money Exchange Shop Owners' Association has issued a notification to its members warning them to refrain from acting as agents in this connection.

It is understood that the Association will hold an oath-taking ceremony against dealing in the bogus State's banknotes.

Hwa Mei Wan Pao dated June 5:

PROMINENT WOMEN JOURNEY TO SOOCHOW OVER NATIONAL SALVATION TRIAL

Mesdames Sun Yat-sen and Liao Chung-kai and 14 others, including one Miss Chen Pu-erh (陳波兒), a local movie star, left here by train for Soochow at 8 a.m. July 5 for the purpose of calling upon Mr. Chu Shih-sung (朱樹聲), the President, and Mr. Sung Hung-ling (宋洪齡), the Chief Procurator of the Kiangsu High Court, in connection with the case against Sung Chun-tz (沈鈞儒) and the six other national salvation leaders.

They returned to Shanghai the same night.

The "Tien Hsia Daily News" reports that the motive of Mesdames Sun Yat-sen and Liao Chung-kai in paying a visit to the President of the Kiangsu High Court was to request him to place them under detention should Sung Chun-tz and the six other leaders of the National Salvation Association be found guilty.

June 29, 1937. Afternoon Translation

Hwa Mei Wan Pao dated June 28 published the following special correspondence from Tientsin :-

CHINESE TRAITOR RECEIVES IMPORTANT POSITION IN NORTH CHINA

Liu Kwei-tong (刘桂堂), a notorious traitor, has recently been appointed by the Japanese Kwantung Army as Commander-in-Chief of the Bogus Anti-Red Forces in North China. He left Tientsin for Northern Chahar on June 26 in company with two Japanese for the purpose of establishing his headquarters. He was issued by the Japanese Kwantung Army with the huge sum of $600,000 which will be used exclusively for the purpose of enrolling bandits from various places in North China as a means of counter-attack against the People's Self-Defence Forces in North Chahar. He was recommended to the Japanese Kwantung Army by a Japanese named Miura, Chairman of the Anti-Red Hsin Loong Association in North China.

In Tientsin, traitors Bai Chien-ho (白坚武) and Heh Pang (郝鹏) are engaged in activities for the enrolling of disgruntled military officers. With a view to averting public attention to their activities, they are using the French Park in the French Concession in Tientsin as the place for assembly and discussions. Both of them are in the pay of the Japanese Kwantung Army.

Kuo Min Weekly (国民周刊), Volume 1, Issue No. 8, published the following article :-

THE NATIONAL SALVATION TRIAL

Two weeks have elapsed since the petition was submitted by the seven national salvation leaders for the withdrawal of the Judges. The prosecution, however, has still not finished its case and it is known that proceedings will continue on June 25. What will be the outcome of the second hearing of the case, we are at present not in a position to foretell. However, in our opinion, unless the Judges charged with this case are prejudiced, there is no alternative for them but to find the accused not guilty.

The statements made by the accused at the first hearing of the case clearly point in this direction and are a sufficient proof that it was entirely due to their patriotism that the seven accused formed the national salvation association Not only are they not opposed to the administration of the National Government, but they also advocate strongly the unification of the country under the guidance of the Government for the rejuvenation of the nation. Should they have unfavourably criticized the Government in the past for its policy, they are now, however, quite in sympathy with the Government's active policy. On the other hand, it is likewise possible for the Government to be lenient towards them even if some of their past activities are regarded as irregular, especially at this time when the whole nation is unanimously united.

In short, the final outcome of this case will constitute a test of the internal unification of China. We firmly believe that it will bring about good and satisfactory results.

June 28, 1937.

MAINICHI

THE TRIAL OF THE SEVEN ARRESTED LEADERS

The Mainichi publishes the
following articles:-
The trial of the seven arrested
leaders of the anti-Japanese popular front movement continued
at the Kiangsu High Court on June 25. The prisoners
denied connection with the Communist Party, the Sian incident
and the instigation of Japanese cotton mill strikes though
they admitted that they were anti-Japanese in sentiment.
The important point to be discussed
in the trial is neither the formation of the anti-Japanese
National Salvation Association nor the agitation of the
Japanese cotton mill strike but their activities relating
to the Sian incident. Prior to the Sian incident they
sent a telegram to General Chang Hsueh-liang advising him
to force General Chiang Kai-shek who was in Shensi at that
time, to take anti-Japanese action by means of military strength.
This is a true fact and it leads us to believe that the
accused were connected with the communist party. The
telegraphic suggestion to General Chang Hsueh-liang alone
is enough to constitute a felony which deserves the highest
degree of punishment. The trial is much concerned with
the accused's attitude towards General Chiang Kai-shek.
For this reason, the C. C. Corps and the Blue Shirts Society,
which have been active to strengthen Chiang Kai-shek's
regime at any cost, will undoubtedly be interested. It
will be a difficult matter for the judges as the hand of the
C. C. Corps can be clearly seen behind the Kiangsu High
Court.
The case of the seven arrested
leaders is evidence of the dispute between the National
Government and the Communist Party even after they had
agreed to co-operate. If this dispute grows as the
national unification work progresses it will be a great
danger to the rehabilitation of China.

Morning Translation

Statement of Sung Chun-dz

The following were questions put to Sung Chun-dz
by the Presiding Judge:-
Q: When was the Shanghai Cultural Circles National Salvation
Association inaugurated?
A: In December, 1935.
Q: How many Standing Committee members have the Shanghai
Cultural Circles National Salvation Association: Were
you one of the Standing Committee members?
A: I do not remember now many there were. I was one of them.
Q: When was the Shanghai Various Circles National Salvation
Association inaugurated?
A: At the time of commemorating the anniversary of the
January 28 Incident, in 1936.
Q: Does the Shanghai Various Circles National Salvation
Association include the Vocational Circles National
Salvation Association, the Cultural Circles National
Salvation Association, the Womens Circles National
Salvation Association and the National Crisis Education
Society?
A: Yes, also a Professors' National Salvation Association.
Q: When and where was the All-China National Salvation
Federation inaugurated?
A: On May 31 last year at the Youths' Federation.
Q: What was the object of the National Salvation Association?
A: Very simple, to resist Japan and save the nation. There
was no other object than to resist Japan.
Q: Were the manifesto and the general principles issued by
the All-China National Salvation Federation passed by
the general meeting?
A: Yes.
Q: Who drafted them?
A: Many persons.
Q: Were you among them?
A: Yes.
Q: What were the contents of the manifesto?
A: It beseeched all the parties and cliques in the country
to discard their prejudices and resist Japan under the
leadership of the Government.
Q: What was the idea of the general principles?
A: They were a sort of suggestion made from the people's
standpoint with the hope that the various parties and
cliques would unite to resist Japan.
Q: What was the difference between the terms "people's front"
and "people's national salvation front" used by you?
A: The two terms had different meanings. "People's front"
is one for dealing with internal affairs. For instance,
the people's fronts of France and Spain were formed to
oppose Fascism in these countries. The "people's national
salvation front," on the other hand, advocated the
unification of the country against aggression by the alien
enemy. Furthermore, we never used the term "people's front."
In July last year Tseu Tao-fun wrote an article in the paper
instructing readers not to use the term "people's front"
so as to avoid misunderstandings. In the charge, this
term was cited to accuse us falsely; this is not correct.
Q: You said all parties and cliques should unite. Which
parties and cliques did you mean?

3
June 26, 1937. Morning Translation

A: The parties meant the Kuomintang, the Communist Party
and the so-called Third Party. The clique meant the
Nationalism Clique. I was a member of the Kuomintang.
Q: By suggesting the cessation of internal strife, do you
oppose the campaign for the suppression of Communists?
A: We are of the opinion that internal friction greatly
diminishes national strength. At that time, the situation
in Kwangtung and Kwangsi was very tense; therefore, we
suggested all parties and cliques should join hands to
offer resistance against Japan.
Q: By suggesting the release of political offenders, do
you mean the Communists?
A: It does not mean the Communists in particular; it means
all those who have been arrested for holding different
political views. For the past few years we have adhered
to this suggestion. For instance, at several meetings
held by the Central Executive Committee of the Kuomintang,
some C.E.C. members had also submitted the same proposal.
Q: The general principles issued by the All-China National
Salvation Federation advocate the introduction of various
parties and cliques to hold a conference. What does this
mean and how is the introduction to be effected?
A: This is simply a suggestion to the various parties and
cliques with the intention to discuss ways and means to
resist Japan.
Q: The general principles advocate the formation of a united
political power of resistance against the enemy. Does it
not mean a re-organization of the Government?
A: No. By the so-called unification, it means that the
Government unifies all the parties and cliques and that
the people, under the leadership of the Government, offer
resistance against Japan. By this, we support the
Government and not oppose it.
Q: What is the guarantee for all the parties and cliques to

A: The National Salvation Association is not a political
party; it is meant to unite the various forces together
against external aggression.
Q: It is said in the general principles that sanctions will
be applied against any party which commits a breach. How
are the sanctions to be applied?
A: We suggest that the National Government lead the nation
in the resistance against Japan. If any party fails to
obey, only the National Government will exercise the
authority.
Q: Will the Communists abandon their principles by offering
resistance against Japan?
A: This is a matter concerning the Communists and has nothing
to do with the National Salvation Association. In the
past, certain people said that the Communists would not
abandon their principles to offer resistance against
Japan. But the facts prove that after the Sian Coup
the Communists were willing to give up their former
policies of class struggles and unanimously offer
resistance against Japan. This is what the people
expect and furthermore whether or not to ally with the

4
June 26, 1937. Morning Translation

Q: The Communists have principles of their own and it is feared that it is not easy to secure alliance with them.
A: By alliance, we mean resistance against Japan, and we do not talk of principles.
Q: The pamphlets issued by four of you advocate alliance with the various parties and cliques, particularly the Communists. What does this mean?
A: Besides the Kuomintang, the Communist Party is naturally one of the biggest political cliques in China. The Kuomintang, however, occupies the highest rank.
Q: How do you know that the Communist Party has expressed resistance against Japan?
A: We have read about it in the newspapers.
Q: When was Mau Shih-tung's letter received?
A: About June or July last year.

Q: Is the Fire Flower Reading Society (火花讀书会) a communist organization?
A: I do not know. There is no such body participating in the National Salvation Association.

A: We did nothing of the sort. We did not know until we read about it in the newspapers.
Q: Had the National Salvation Association any part in the suspension of studies in Shanghai?
A: I request to be enlightened as to which particular event.
Q: December, 1935.
A: Where? Since the Presiding Judge asks us, of course he has the proof. Please show it.
Q: Did you know Lu Tsing (羅青) at the home of Tseu Tao-fun?
A: I have not seen him. The charge sheet states that I knew him at Tsang Nai-chi's home. Which is the actual place, at Tseu Tao-fun's or at Tsang Nai-chi's? Q: You all demand that an investigation be made concerning Chang Hsuch-liang. What is the reason for this?

Q: What else do you want investigated?
A: There are many things. A statement was submitted to the Court yesterday, containing more than ten points regarding the manifesto issued at the time of the Third Plenary Congress and other matters. As to matters regarding the suspension of studies by students, the Court is requested to quote facts.

June 26, 1937.
Morning Translation.

June 26, 1937.
Morning Translation.

Q: Is there not the phrase "the establishment of an anti-Japanese political regime" mentioned in the manifesto and the general principles of the All-China National Salvation Federation?

But, whether or not the Communist Party was determined to resist Japan I do not know. Even the Presiding Judge and Procurator, I fear, could not know it. It is too unreasonable that the establishment of an anti-Japanese political regime as mentioned by our Federation should be alleged to have connection with the establishment of a national defence government as proposed by the Communist Party.
Q: Do you advocate the toleration of Communism?

A: The Communist Party will not abandon its Communism. What shall we do if the Communists create disturbances at the rear?
A: We have the strength of our people to suppress them.
Q: Do you know that you have been made use of by the Communist Party?

A: 13 years ago, Dr. Sun Yat-sen advocated the toleration of Communism. Is it true that Dr. Sun Yat-sen was also wrong? No. But the alliance with the Communists depends upon the circumstances. 10

Here the Procurator of the Court rose and stated:

Sz Liang: I am a Committee member of the Women's Circles National Salvation Association. Judge: Where is the All-China Various Circles National Association established?
As It is established in the Youths' Federation.

As During the National Crisis Conference held four years ago, we had already maintained the opinion of uniting all parties and cliques. After the outbreak of the South-west embroglio last year, we felt great anxiety at the sight of the daily dwindling of our territory, while internal unity had still not yet been achieved after the loss of several provinces. For this reason, we started to renew the manifesto of the National Crisis Conference to push forward the demand for unifying all parties and cliques, and of no more fighting among our own people. We should unite to resist Japan for the salvation of our country. To speak the truth, the Communists are Chinese people also; comparing the Communists with the Japanese Imperialists, the latter are naturally a worse enemy to us. THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, JUNE 20, 1937

Salvationists' Trial
To Resume In Soochow

Trial of the seven All-China National Salvation Association leaders on charges of endangering the state will be resumed in the Kiangsu High Court in Soochow with Judge Chu Tsung-chow presiding at 9 o'clock in the morning of June 26, according to reliable reports received here late last night.

The application was accepted and Judge Chu Tsung-chow of the second section of the criminal division was appointed to preside at the hearing. Immediately upon appointment, Judge Chu proceeded with studying the voluminous files in connection with the case. The study will be completed before June 26 when the trial will be resumed.

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Friday, June 18, 1937

New Judge Named
In Patriot Case

Re-Trial Now Probable
At Soochow; Accused
Remain In Cells

Granting the application by the seven All-China National Salvation Association leaders for appointment of new judges to preside over their trial on charge of undermining the security of the state, the Kiangsu High Court in Soochow has appointed Chief Judge Chu Chung-chow of the second section of the criminal division to handle the hearing. It was officially announced in Soochow last night.

As result of the change in the judges, the trial, which opened in Soochow a week ago, is expected to be heard all over again. As Chief Judge Chu has to study the voluminous files in connection with the case, the first session under the new judge may not take place until early in July.

Charges Made

The seven leaders of the All-China National Salvation Association filed the application for the appointment of new judges last Saturday following the prolonged first session on the previous day. They charged the presiding judge with being prejudiced and biased inasmuch as he overruled numerous applications by the accused to investigate evidence and witnesses which they consider as favorable to the defense.

The accused also took strong exception to the action by the previous judges in ordering the first hearing to be held in camera. It was through their concerted threat to boycott the judges and to refuse answering their questions that two members of their families and the press representatives were finally allowed to enter the courtroom.

Spend Days In Jail

With no date set for the resumption of the momentous trial, the accused are spending their days in the detention house in Soochow. Messrs. Shen Chung-ju, Sah Chien-li, Li Kung-po, Chang Nai-chi, Tsou Tao-feng and Wang Chao-shih, the six male members of the now famous "Seven Gentlemen" are in their special "suite" while Miss Sze Liang, the woman lawyer, has a room to herself in the female detention house. Of the three others who also are standing trial, only Lo Tsing is detained. Two others, junior members of the National Salvation Association, were allowed released on bail.

The movement to request the early release of the seven leaders and the three followers grows in Shanghai today. The latest public body to request the release of its members involved in the case is the Chinese Bar Association. In a meeting of the executive committee of the Association, it was decided to send a petition to the National Government requesting the early release of Shen Chung-ju, Sah Chien-li, Wong Chao-shih, and Miss Sze Liang. Mr. Shen is a member of the standing committee of the Association. During the meeting, an article written by Mr. Shen in the Soochow detention house on the fund campaign for the construction of a new building for the Association was approved. The article is to be engraved on the cornerstone of the new building.

The following is the text of their reply
to the prosecution, submitted to the Kiangsu High Court
at Soochow, which was jointly drafted by their lawyers:-

Facts of the Offence and Evidence

The accused in this case, noticing the
gravity of the national crisis, were in sorrow at the
imminent downfall of China. Their patriotism is not beyond
that shown by other fellow countrymen. At that time, both
the National Salvation Association and the accused were of
the opinion that the only alternative to avert national
extinction was to bring about unification of the people
throughout the country as a means of resistance against
outside aggression. For this reason, their speeches and
activities were all directed in this movement. The reason
why they advocated peaceful unification and concentration
of national strength was purely for the purpose of bringing
about the attainment of this object. All this can be
verified by the following items of this reply, that deal
with the National Salvation Association and the personal
correspondence and documents of the various accused concerned.
Later, the antagonistic feelings against
the enemy of the people throughout the country became more
and more energetic. Such a tendency among the people of
the country has brought strong support to the diplomatic
negotiations and policy of the Government, resulting in
the frustration of the plots of the traitorous elements,
the aversion of a serious crisis in North China, the
adoption of a stronger attitude in the Government's diplomatic
negotiations with Japan and a slight diminution in the
arrogant attitude of the enemy. However, just at the time
when the accused were regretting that their strength for
national salvation was too weak and that they had not yet
completed 1/100th of their duty towards their nation, they
were arrested one after another in the International
Settlement and the French Concession in Shanghai at mid-
night on November 22 last year, and were subsequently
charged in accordance with Article 6 of the Law Governing
Punishment of Persons Who Commit Acts With Intent To Injure
the Republic of China.

The Items of the Reply

According to Article 6 of the Law Governing
Punishment of Persons Who Commit Acts With Intent To Injure
the Republic of China, whoever is suspected of having
organized associations, held meetings or propagated a
doctrine irreconcilable with the Three Principles of the
People shall be punishable.
Whether the object of the National Salvation
Association is for the purpose of working for the salvation
of the nation or otherwise or whether the doctrine it
propagated is irreconcilable with the Three Principles of
the People or otherwise does not merit discussion. The
prosecution brought against the accused by the Kiangsu High
Court, though it contains 10 points dealing with the evidence
for this prosecution lacks sound and thorough understanding
and observation of the circumstances and evidence of this case.

It is only a misinterpretation of the various documents
of the National Salvation Association. With a view to
clearing off this misconception, the following items of
the reply are submitted:-
(1) In the First Item of the prosecution,
it was alleged that the accused were intentionally obstruct-
ing the national policy of the Central Government towards
uprooting the Red Menace.
The National Salvation Association was
inaugurated for the purpose of dealing with Japan. The
question of Soviet Russia and the Communist Party has
nothing to do with the object and the principle of the
Association. As the prosecution lacks thorough understanding
of the contents of the various documents it referred to as
regards problems dealing with Japan, what the prosecution
alleged cannot, therefore, be regarded as sound and concrete.
It may be recalled that each time the proposal for a Sino-
Japanese joint operation against Reds was brought up for
discussion by Japan during the Sino-Japanese parleys held
at Nanking last year, it was rejected by the National
Government. From this, it can be seen that the policy
of the National Salvation Association towards the Red problem
is not inconsistent with that of the Government. That the
prosecution alleges that the accused were intentionally
obstructing the national policy of the Government towards
uprooting the Red menace indicates that it lacks sound
understanding of the true policy of the National Government.
(2) In the Second Item of the prosecution,
the accused were alleged to have recklessly attacked the
present Government, disregarding its controlling power.
It must be noted that the National Salvation
Association advocated unanimous unification throughout the
country because of the increasing aggression through alien
invasion. Such a tendency of the Association cannot be
taken as evidence for offence, especially in view of the
fact that the Government is earnestly desirous of peaceful
unification. As regards the terms "resistance against the
enemy" and "the salvation of the nation" contained in the
expressions "a unified political power for resistance against
the enemy" and "a unified political power for the salvation
of the nation," they constitute the unanimous demands of
the people throughout the country. For this reason, it
was recognized at that time that so long as the Government
could express its determination for resistance against the
enemy and for the salvation of the nation, it would be easy
for the Government to unify its political power. Moreover,
only when the Government possesses a unified political
power, will it be able successfully to carry out its
resistance against the enemy for the salvation of the nation.
The object and the method of the National Salvation
Association for advocating peaceful unification as mentioned
in the manifesto issued by the National Salvation Federation
of Various Circles Throughout the Country is quite in
conformity with the policy of General Chiang Kai-shek. It
is indispensable to bring about a unified political power
in order to resist the enemy and to avert national extinction,
while to bring about peace in the country constitutes the
principal path for the realization of such a unified
political power, and the admission of members of all parties
and cliques to a conference to decide upon measures for
resistance against the enemy is the only way to bring about
a peaceful unification.

thorough study of the circumstances of the case has been

not known previously of the existence of this paper. It
was only after he had been told by his friend that in
this paper there were articles about him and Tsang Nai-chi
that he asked his friend to get a copy for his perusal.
This is how the paper came into his possession.
(8) In the Ninth Item of the prosecution,
the Sian Incident was taken as reference to allege that
the accused had conspired with military leaders in carrying
out subversive activities. But it must be noted that the
Sian Mutiny broke out on December 12 last year, while the
accused had already been arrested on November 22 the same
year. At the time of the outbreak of the incident, they
were held in custody in the detention house of the Kiangsu
High Court at Soochow. Not only were they unable to
conspire with outsiders, but they were also ignorant of
the affair. As regards the demand made by General Chang
Hsueh-liang for the release of the accused, it must be
noted that the activities of General Chang had nothing to
do with the accused who had already been held in detention
for 20 days at that time. Moreover, it was General Chang
alone in this country who asked for the release of these
accused. From a logical point of view, it is, therefore,
unreasonable to allege on such evidence that the accused
conspired with military leaders for subversive activities.
(9) In the Tenth Item of the prosecution,
Tsang Nai-chi, Sung Chun-tz and Tseu Tao-fun were
implicated in the activities of Lo Ching (羅青), who
was held as having participated in an organization the
intent of which was to injure the Republic of China.
It must be noted that Tsang Nai-chi never
detailed Lo Ching to undertake the responsibility for the
formation of any National Salvation Association, nor did
the National Salvation Federation of the Various Circles
Throughout the Country send out any representative to
organize any organizations. Moreover, the various National
Salvation Associations in the various other places were
established by the persons at those places. They are not

members of the National Salvation Federation of the
Various Circles Throughout the Country, therefore they
have not had any affiliations with the Federation.
In view of the foregoing explanations,
it can be seen that the national salvation work undertaken
by the accused was for the purpose of urging the entire
nation to adopt an unanimous resistance against alien
invasion. Their work is quite in conformity with the
past as well as the present policies of the National
Government. It appears that the prosecution lacks
thorough understanding of the motive of the National
Salvation Association and the national policy of the
Government, and therefore none of the evidence it contained
can stand.
The Kiangsu High Court is, therefore,
requested to deal with the case impartially and to acquit
the accused so as to uphold justice. The Court is also
requested to cease detention of the accused so as to
enable them to attend hearings of the case whenever
required.

Facts of the Offence and Evidence

Dissatisfied with the administration of the
present Government, Sung Chun-dz, Wong Zao-dz, Li Kung-poh,
Soo Chi-li, Tsang Naŋ-chi, Tseu Tao-fun, Sz Liang and Dao

April 7, 1937. Afternoon Translation.

Ying-ts (who is still at large), under the pretext of resisting the enemy and alien aggression by the unification of various Parties and circles, promoted the People's Front for National Salvation. At first they organized a body known as the National Salvation Association of the Cultural Circles, Professional Circles and Women's Circles. Later, in collaboration with the University Professors' National Salvation Association, the Students' National Salvation Association, the Workers' National Salvation Association, the National Crisis Educational Society and various other bodies, they organized the National Salvation Federation of the Various Circles of Shanghai and started the publication of printed matter as a means of extending its influence and attraction.

Not long afterwards, they extended the sphere of the Federation and formed the National Salvation Federation of the Various Circles Throughout the Country. On May 31 of the 25th Year of the Chinese Republic (1936), they held an inauguration meeting of this Federation at the Young Men's Federation in the International Settlement of Shanghai and at the same time issued a manifesto dealing with the inauguration meeting of the Federation and the Preliminary Political Principles dealing with National Salvation and Resistance against Japan. On July 15 of the same year (1936), Sung Chun-dz, Tsang Na-chi, Dao Ying-ts, and Tseu Tao-fun published a pamphlet under the caption "Several Fundamental Conditions and Our Minimum Demands for Resistance Against Alien Invasion by Unification", advocating cessation of internal strife, release of political offenders, compromise with the Red Army and establishment of a united political Government for resistance against the enemy.

Having read in the newspapers the speeches delivered by Sung Chun-dz and others, Mou Cheh-tung (毛澤東), leader of the communist bandits who were then retreating in the North-west, sent a reply addressed to Sung Chun-dz and others in favour of their suggestions. Upon receipt of this favourable support, Sung Chun-dz and others, considering that they had attained their object, worked more energetically for the enlargement of their influence, and detailed Lo Ching, another accused, to undertake the formation of the National Salvation Federation of the Various Circles of Kiangsu Province. Henceforth, their activities became more and more energetic. At the same time, they started the publication of a paper known as "National Extinction Aversion Intelligence Report", strongly criticising the administrative policies of the National Government in the hope of reducing the people's confidence in the Government.

Taking advantage of the strike of workers that was then in progress in the various Japanese cotton mills in Shanghai, Sung Chun-dz and others formed a body known as the "Strikes Support Committee" and started the collection of contributions for financial support of the strikers, with the intention of urging the strikers to undertake activities coincident with those of the National Salvation Federation. For this reason, they (Sung Chun-dz, Wong Zao-dz, Soo Chi-li, Li Kung-poh, Tsang Na-chi, Tseu Tao-fun and Sz Liang) were arrested by the Shanghai Bureau of Public Safety, now known as the Shanghai City Government Police Bureau, with the assistance of the Police authorities of the International Settlement and the French Concession in Shanghai.

April 7, 1937. Afternoon Translation.

With the exception of Sz Liang, who disappeared
after release on bail, the arrested persons were handed
over, together with certain evidence, to this Court for
investigations as they were suspected of having conspired
with communist elements, organized illegitimate bodies
and instigated strikes of workers and students, with the
intention of menacing public peace and order as well as
overthrowing the Government. Later, Sz Liang surrendered
herself to this Court during the progress of the investiga-
tions that were being conducted by this Court. Later,
Lo Ching was arrested in Kiangying and was handed to this
Court by the Military Court of the Military Affairs
Commission.

During the time when the investigations into
this case were still in progress, Koo Liu-hsiang, Zung
Chung-kao, Chang Chung-mei, Chen Tao-hung and Chen Tso,
as representatives from the National Salvation Federation
of the Various Circles of Shanghai, submitted a petition
to this Court requesting the release of Sung Chun-dz and
others. In view of the fact that these persons were all
members of the National Salvation Association of the
Professional Circles of Shanghai, moreover, as Zung Chung-
kao was the Secretary of this Association, they must have
had connections with the communists; they were therefore
likewise held in detention by this Court pending investi-
gations. As a result of these investigations, it was
ascertained that the principal object of the various accused
in establishing such bodies and propagating doctrines that
were contrary to the Three Principles of the People was to
endanger the internal security of the Republic of China.
The evidence for the prosecution is as
follows:-

(1) In the manifesto issued by the National
Salvation Federation of Various Circles Throughout the
Country, it states: "The attacks made on Soviet Russia by
various Powers are unjustified, while bandit suppression
in China is also wrongful," and "A small number of people
with ulterior motives still regard the Soviet Union and the
Communist Party as the principal enemies of the Chinese
people."

Similar statements have also frequently
been published in the Salvation Bulletin. It must be clear
to all that the Communist Party has done serious damage
to the country. The object of the Communist Party is
inconsistent with that of the Three Principles of the People.
The accused formed an organization proposing that no
punitive action be taken against the Communist Party and
openly criticising the bandit suppression policy of the
Government; it is very obvious that they were intentionally
obstructing the national policy of the Central Government
towards uprooting the Red menace.

(2) Besides advocating that political
offenders be immediately released, the above mentioned
manifesto also states that "The various parties and cliques
should formally send their respective representatives and
the People's Front for National Salvation is willing to
arrange a general principle for joint resistance against
the enemy and to establish a unified political power to
resist the enemy". The Anti-Japanese National Salvation
Preliminary Political Principles also demand that "A unified
national salvation political power be immediately established."
From this evidence, it is clear that the
accused took similar steps to these

Defence Government of the Unified Country".
As the accused are under the control of
the National Government and Sung Chung-dz and Lo Ching also
called themselves "Kuomintang members", and as they know

(3) In the various publications issued by
Sung Chun-dz, Tsang Nan-chi, Dao Ying-ts and Tseu Tao-fun
suggesting the several fundamental conditions and minimum
demands for a unification against aggressors, the following
sentences are found:
"To make a truce with the Red Army for a
joint resistance against Japan," "The so-called various

"Recently the Communist Party proposed a joint resistance
against Japan, but the Kuomintang made no comment at all;

Furthermore, when asked by this Court that

the Great Wall, the Red Army took advantage of the situation
by making a counter attack at the rear, how can the Red

there that no similar action will be taken by the Communist
Party afterwards?", the accused could not give a reasonable

According to Li Kung-poh's statement, "From
what I read in newspapers and magazines, the Communist Party
is anti-Japanese, but whether it is determined to resist

aggressors. The accused placed the Kuomintang and the
Government among various other parties and cliques, and at
the same time, they maintained that the so-called "various

Communist Party." This proves that they despised the present Government

On the one hand, the accused point to the bandit suppression

The reply given by Mr. "Ma-Ke-Lai-Li" contains only four words: "Friends are in distress".

Miss Sze Liang(史良), the female lawyer, has so far failed to put in an appearance after she was released on the guarantee of her lawyers, Messrs Chang Tse Niang(張志讓) and Tong Hao(唐豪). The Procuratorate of the Kiangsu Third Branch High Court has issued a circular warrant for her arrest and has bound over the two lawyers on cash securities of $500 each and ordered them to locate Miss Sze Liang within ten days.
It is learned that the two lawyers and the family of Miss Sze Liang have done their best to locate her but without success. Miss Sze Liang's mother has become ill since receiving a letter from her daughter in which she stated that she would not return.
Yesterday the two lawyers published advertisements in the local newspapers advising Miss Sze Liang to appear in Court. A similar advertisement was also published by Miss Sze Liang's brothers and sisters.

Made by D.S. Jones Forwarded by. [签名]

With reference to the inquiry dated November 25, 1935
from the Acting Consul General for Belgium concerning the
present whereabouts of Mr Leon Terrie, I have to state that
this individual has now left Shanghai for Europe.
According to information procured from Melchers & Co.,
No. 210 Kiukiang Road, Terrie was signed on in this port as a
member of the crew of the Norddeutscher Lloyd steamship HAVEL,
prior to her departure to Japan on October 23, 1935. After
visiting certain ports in Japan this vessel returned to
Shanghai and on November 14th steamed out of Shanghai on the
homeward voyage to Hamburg. Terrie was still on board when the
vessel departed for the second time and is believed to be
working his passage to Europe in the capacity of ship's fireman.

VARIOUS CIRCLES NATIONAL SALVATION ASSOCIATION 
HOLDS DEMONSTRATION IN FRENCH CONCESSION 


On June 12 the Kiangsu High 
Court held the second hearing of the case against the seven 
Jenders of the maticnal salvation movement. 
The Shanghai Various Circles 
National Salvation Association issued a notification to 
various public bodies in Shanghai to the effect that at 
3 pem. June 13 a demonstration would be held on a piece of 
vacant ground on Route de Zikawei, French Concession, to 
demand the release of the seven arrested leaders. About 
5000 students and labourers assembled at the appointed 
time and held a demonstration under a preeiding board of 
five professors. 
Acting on information, the French 
Police dispatched a number of policemen to the scene to deal 
with the situation. 
The chairman of the demonstration 
» during the course of his speech, said that the seven leaders 
were reported to have been sentenced to 5 years' imprisonment, 
He further said that if such patriots were to be condemned 
all Chinese people would be condemned because of tneir love 
of patriotic movements. For this reason, the people 
should strongly demand the release of the seven leaders. 
This speech was followed by a loud cry from the 5000 
demonstrators that the Government should release the seven 
leaders immediately. 
The follov ing resolutions were 
passed:- 
1. That the trial of the seven leaders be cancelled and 
the prisoners released immediately. 
2. That patriotic movements be protected. 
3. That the freedom of speech and organization be protected, 
4. That democratic administration be practised. 
5. That all political prisoners be released. 
6. That Japanese goods be boycotted and smuggling be 
suppressed by armed force. 
7. That the Government be supported and an anti-Japanese 
front be formed inmediately. 
8. That the East Hopei Autonomous Government be cancelled 
and the lost territory be recovered. 
9. That China's entire population be armed and stirred up. 
10. That the Government issue an order to the peaple to 
organize national salvation associations. 
11. That the Government should finance the North-East 
University. 
12. That diplomatic affairs be open to the public. 
13. That all pro-Japanese government officers be dismissed. 
The demonstration was dispersed at 5 pem. due to the 
rain and the efforts of the French Police. 
A large number of inflammatory anti~Japanese handbills 
were distributed among the demonstrators. 
The handbill contains the following 
slogans :- 
1. The Government should unite with the people to resist 
enemies and save the country. 
2- Celebrate in advance the relesse of the seven leaders 
and the release of political prisoners. 
3. Arrest of patriots must be discontinued and patriotic 
movements must not be interfered with. 
4e Freedom and equality ¢ the people must be practised and 
mational independence must be completed.

While conscious of our obligation, as a 

foreign journal in China, not to indulge in 
undue tendering of advice or critical activity 
toward the nation which is our host, we feel 
it proper to note that yesterday's Ta Kung 
Pao remarked upon ‘the same event in a 
frame of mind comparable to that of 
“Liberal”. 
"Tn Tact that outspoken journal was dis. 
tinctly opposed to the attitude of the authori- 
ties in detaining the six without complying | 
with Chinese legal requirements to a hearing 
within 24 hours of arrest. It declared itself 
strongly on behaif of the civil rights of the 
individual, and {f any official view to the 
contrary has manifested itself, the fact has 
not come to our attention. 

More pleasant, however, is the fact that 
gocd treatment is apparently being accorded 
the six. They are said to be incarcerated in. 
two comfortable roéms vastly better than 
prison cells, near the office of headquarters 
of the Bureau of Public Safety; special con- 
sideration is reported to be accorded them, 
and they are given sudh privileges as the} 
chance to smoke and play games. In other 
words the authorities seem to be merely 
keeping them “out of circulation” while in- 
dulging in none of the horrors which have 
been features of some past acts against 
Leftists. 

Clearly the authorities felt themselves 
entitled to resort to extraordinary measures 
to deal with an extreordinary situation. The 
Salvationists sought to capitalize strike 
troubles in local Japanese cotton mills in 
connection with the Butyuan warfare, and the 
authorities feared international complications. 

While the . reported good treatment is 
praiseworthy as far @s it goes, the whole 
affair is clearly extra-legal. Therefore it is 
damaging to China’s reputation for living by 
her own laws. —

July 8, 1937. Morning Translatione 


Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers (Soochow Telegram) :- 


THE CASE AGAINST THE NATIONAL SALVATION LEADERS : PERIOD 
FOR THEIR DETENTION EXTENDED 


Sung Chun-dz (AH, 441% ) and the six 
Others ,who are charged with offerices against internal 
Security of the State, received on July 6 the following 
judgment from the Kiangsu High Court as regards the 
extension of their detention period:- 

"The accused in this case, who are 
charged with offences against the internal security of 
the Republic, have been under detention in this Court 
since April 5 last. However, despite the fact that the 
three months' detention period has expired, the 
investigation into the evidence of this case is still 
incomplete and it is, therefore, necessary to prolong 
the period of the detention of the accused. Consequently, 
the period of their detention is extended for a further 
period of two months as from July 5 in accordance with 
the provisions of Article 108, Sections 1 and 2, of the 
Code of Criminal Procedure." 

Upon receipt of this judgment, the 
accused requested the Kiangsu High Court to resume the 
hearing of the case as soon ag possible on the ground 
that they had already been under detention for a 
considerable length of time.

Two weeks have elapsed since the 
petition Was submitted by the seven national salvation 
leaders for the withdrawal of the Judges. The prosecution, 
however, has still not finished its case and it is known 
that proceedings will eontinue on June 25. What will be 
the outoome of the second hearing of the oase, we are 
at present not in a position to foretell. However, in 
our opinion, unless the Judges charged with this case are 
prejudiced, there is no alternative for them but to find 
the accused not guilty. 

The statements made by the accused at 
the first hearing of the oase clearly point in this 
direction and are a sufficient proéf that it was entirely 
due to their patriotism that the seven accused formed 
the national salvation association Not only are they 
not opposed to the administration of the National Government, 
but they also advogate strongly the unification of the 
country under the guidance of the Government for the 
rejuvenation of the nation. Should they have unfavourably 
oriticized the Government in the past for its policy, they 
are now, however, quite in sympathy with the Government's 
active policy. On the other hand, it is likewise possible 
for the Government to be lenient towards them even if some 
of their past activities are regarded as irregular, 
eae at this time when the whole nation is unanimously 
un ede 

In short, the final outcome of this case 
will constitute a test of the internal unification of China- 
We firmly believe that it will bring about good and 
Batisfactory results.

THE TRIAL OF THE SEVEN ARRESTED LEADERS 


The Mainichi publishes the 
following articles<- 

The trial of the seven arrested 
leaders of the anti-Japanese popular front movement continued 
at the Kiangsu High Court on June 25. The prisoners 
denied connection with the Communist Party, the Sian incident 
and the instigation of Japanese cotton mill strikes though 
they admitted that they were anti-Japanese in sentiment. 

The important point to be discussed 
in the trial is neither the formation of the anti-Japanese 
Wational Salvation Association nor the agitation of the 
Japanese cotton mill strike but their activities relating 
to the Sian incident. Prior to the Sian incident they 
sent a telegram to General Chang 4sueh-liang advising him 
to force General Chiang Kai-shek who was in Shensi at that 
time, to takeanti-Japanese action by means of military strength. 
This is a true fact and it leads us to believe that the 
accused were connected with the communist party. The 
telegraphic suggestion to General Chang Hsueh-liang alone 
is enough to constitute a felony which deserves the highest 
degree of punishment. The trial is much concerned with 
the accused's attitude towards General Chiang Kai-shek. 

For this reason, the C. C. Corps and the Blue Shirts Society, 
which have been active to strengthen Chiang Kai-shek's 
regime at any cost, will undoubtedly be interested. It 
will be a difficult matter for the judges as the hand of the 
we Corps can be clearly seen behind the Kiangsu High 

ou e 

The case of the seven arrested 
leaders is evidence of the dispute between the National 
Government and the Communist Party even after they had 
agreed to co-operate. If this dispute grows as the 
national unification work progresses it will be a great 
danger to the rehabilitation of China.
